CredentialsOption.description: One way a discovered device can be paired, with what the UI needs to ask for it.
CredentialsOption.title: CredentialsOption

Device.description:
A device with what its integration keeps about it, ``integration_data``, typed as ``TData``: a bare ``Device``
holds any (a dict once read back), ``class HueDevice(Device[HueData])`` its own model. Unset, it is ``TData``
validated from ``{}`` (the Hub creates a device before its integration pairs it), and stays unset: a save keeps
the stored one. For ``Device[HueData | None]`` that ``{}``, unset or stored, is None.
Device.title: Device

DevicePair.description: Re-pair discovery to the existing device.
DevicePair.title: DevicePair

DeviceParameterChange.description:
A device reported that one of its parameters changed to a new value.

Mirrors :class:`DeviceCommand`'s shape (``device_id``, ``parameter_id``, ``value``) but
flows the other direction — device → Hub.
DeviceParameterChange.title: DeviceParameterChange

DeviceState.description: A device with its parameters' current states, the data of each typed as ``TParameterData``.
DeviceState.title: DeviceState

ErrorOut.description: As the WebSocket tells it (`majordom_did_encounter_error`): whether the integration still runs, its status says.
ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut

IntegrationErrorMessage.description:
A user-facing integration problem. `message` is plain language for display (with any
call-to-action folded into the text); whether the integration still runs, its status says
(IntegrationStatusMessage). Device-scoped problems travel on the device's `last_error` instead.

`id` is stable per condition: a later message with the same `integration` and `id` replaces
this one, and it stays until an IntegrationErrorResolvedMessage with them.
IntegrationErrorMessage.title: IntegrationErrorMessage

IntegrationErrorResolvedMessage.description: The integration's error with this `id` is gone: it cleared, or the integration stopped or restarted.
IntegrationErrorResolvedMessage.title: IntegrationErrorResolvedMessage

IntegrationStatusMessage.description:
An integration's state changed: `kind` says why it waits or failed, for the app to act on. A user-facing error
comes with the states the user can act on (IntegrationErrorMessage).
IntegrationStatusMessage.title: IntegrationStatusMessage

Notification.description:
A general user-facing message an integration surfaces to the user as a floating tile in the
app. Distinct from ``controller_did_encounter_error`` (which is specifically for integration
failures/health) — use this for anything informational or advisory the user should see.

``ttl`` is how many seconds the tile stays before auto-dismissing; ``None`` keeps it until the
user dismisses it.
Notification.title: Notification

NotificationMessage.description:
A general user-facing notification from an integration — rendered as a floating tile. The
nested `notification` carries the message, callout type (info/warning/error), delivery
priority, and ttl. Distinct from IntegrationErrorMessage, which is specifically for failures.
NotificationMessage.title: NotificationMessage

NotificationPriority.description: How insistently the notification is delivered (maps to the OS interruption levels).
NotificationPriority.title: NotificationPriority

NotificationType.description: The callout style the app renders the notification with.
NotificationType.title: NotificationType

ProvidedCredentials.description:
What a pairing request actually supplies — paired with its type, so pairing can
validate it against Discovery.expected_credentials_options instead of trusting
whatever the integration guessed at discovery time.
ProvidedCredentials.title: ProvidedCredentials

StatusKind.description: Why a peripheral waits or failed, for its owner to act on; the status's ``detail`` says it in words.
StatusKind.title: StatusKind

schema.title: Response Get All Automations Api Automation Get
Response Get Discoveries Api Device Discoveries Get

post.description:
Temporarily enables protocol-level discovery mechanisms that are not continuously active. Used to trigger short-lived scan/inquiry modes for transports that require explicit activation
(e.g. Zigbee permit-join style discovery, BLE scan bursts, proprietary radios).

`integration` opens the window of that integration only (every integration's otherwise). `credentials` are the ones
a protocol needs during inclusion, before the device is a discovery (e.g. a Z-Wave device's S2 PIN or QR code):
protocol-specific, so they need `integration`.

delete.description: Soft - keep device in database to skip setup after re-pairing.

schema.title: Response Get Radios Api Hardware Radios Get

post.description:
Switch a radio to another firmware (what it serves); takes about a minute, `is_busy` meanwhile. 409 while it is
busy.

Forget what a radio is; it is identified again while plugged in, up to minutes, `is_busy` meanwhile. 409 while it
is busy.

Identify a plugged-in device that isn't a known radio; opening its port may reset it. Up to minutes, `is_busy`
meanwhile. 409 while it is busy.

schema.title: Response Get Hub Hotspots Api Hub Hotspots Get
Response Is Connected Api Hub Is Connected Get

post.description: Forget everything but the system config; the Hub starts afresh once it answered, ready to be set up again.

Connect the Hub to a Wi-Fi network, with `connect=true`. The network integrations set devices up onto (e.g.
ESPHome over Improv BLE) is chosen in the Hub settings (`PATCH /settings/hub`): without `connect` it's a 400.

schema.title: Response Get Integrations Api Integrations Get

post.description: Stop it until enabled again, across restarts.
Start it anew, one that failed or stopped by itself too.
